title: GL.iNet cloud flaw used to plant malware on routers and KVMs
summary: GL.iNet says an attacker exploited a vulnerability in its GoodCloud remote management service, found on 20 November 2026, to install malware on some GL.iNet routers and KVM-over-IP devices. The cloud flaw is fixed, so devices cannot be newly infected that way, but existing infections are not removed; KVM beta firmware with fixes is out and stable router and KVM firmware was scheduled for 22 November. Researchers quoted by BleepingComputer report root reverse shells and a separate, older persistent backdoor on some devices, which GL.iNet's published check may not detect; GL.iNet has not confirmed how the attack worked or how many devices were hit.
why: GL.iNet KVMs are often plugged into servers and admin workstations for out-of-band access, and travel routers carry admin traffic. A compromised KVM gives keyboard, video and power control of whatever it is attached to, and GL.iNet is still investigating whether connected computers were affected.
todo: Do now: inventory GL.iNet routers and KVMs (including ones staff use for remote or travel work) and note which are bound to GoodCloud.
Run GL.iNet's published indicator check on each device; treat any hit as infected, factory-reset or install the security firmware, and rotate credentials used through it.
If a KVM was infected, check the attached computer for unknown accounts, startup items, scheduled tasks and remote-access tools.
Install the stable security firmware for every model when it is available, and unbind devices from GoodCloud if you do not need cloud management.
Wait for GL.iNet's final scope statement; the older backdoor reports are from researchers and users, not verified by GL.iNet.
effective_note: Incident identified 20 Nov 2026; notice last updated 21 Nov (UTC) — per GL.iNet.

sources.title: BleepingComputer: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
